strategies.overview: Basculegion-M's solid Attack stat, supported by two amazing abilities and high-Base Power STAB moves, makes it one of the most potent wallbreakers available in the tier. An Adaptability-boosted Wave Crash is capable of doing immense damage to bulky walls like Registeel and Swampert and even gets good chip on bulky Water-resistant Pokemon like Milotic and Tsareena. Alternatively, Basculegion-M can opt for Swift Swim on rain teams, becoming an extremely menacing Pokemon that can outspeed and power through bulky and offensive teams alike. While not having much in terms of type coverage, Basculegion-M has access to a solid movepool. Most notably, access to Aqua Jet lets it act as a revenge killer, picking off faster Pokemon such as Cinccino, Infernape, and Munkidori with ease. However, the lack of a reliable physical Ghost-type STAB move hurts Basculegion-M greatly, making it susceptible to Pokemon that it otherwise would have a chance against, namely bulky Water-types such as Vaporeon and Gastrodon. Additionally, Basculegion-M's Speed is rather average, leaving it susceptible to being revenge killed by common Pokemon such as Kilowattrel and Brambleghast as well as Choice Scarf users like Infernape, Rotom-C, and Munkidori as well.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

A mixed attacking Assault Vest set can function as a decent bulky offensive pivot, leveraging Basculegion-M's solid special bulk against common special attackers like Munkidori. However, Basculegion-M's typing leaves it vulnerable to common special attackers such as Chandelure, Kilowattrel, and Rotom-C, making its defensive use somewhat inconsistent. Additionally, the lack of reliable recovery makes it prone to being chipped down over time, forcing it to be paired with a Wish user and making it much less efficient into common threats. Choice Specs Basculegion-M is a decent option, with its stronger coverage options in Shadow Ball and Ice Beam, alongside Adaptability, compensating for its otherwise middling Special Attack stat. This set can threaten typical counterplay to physical Basculegion-M sets such as Vaporeon, Toxicroak, Dragalge, and Amoonguss with either Shadow Ball or Ice Beam.

Checks and Counters

Water-immune Pokemon: Vaporeon is an excellent answer to Basculegion-M thanks to Water Absorb making it immune to Basculegion-M's Water-type STAB moves alongside strong physical bulk with investment making it hardly deterred by any of Basculegion-M's coverage moves. Gastrodon functions similarly, albeit with more reliable recovery with Recover and the ability to turn Basculegion-M's Water-type moves into an opportunity for offensive momentum thanks to Storm Drain. Toxicroak can also switch into Basculegion-M's Water-type moves courtesy of Dry Skin and use Basculegion-M as fodder for setting up Swords Dance. However, Psychic Fangs obliterates Toxicroak, so it must be mindful of Basculegion-M's choice of coverage.

Water- and Dragon-types: Milotic is generally a solid check to Basculegion-M thanks to Recover giving it extremely important longevity as well as Flip Turn letting Milotic use Basculegion-M as a chance to gain momentum. Inteleon can generally switch into Basculegion-M once and, in return, outspeed and OHKO Basculegion-M with Dark Pulse after some chip damage. Dragalge's solid physical bulk lets it come in on Basculegion-M's Water-type STAB moves and either wear it down with Sludge Bomb or finish it off with Draco Meteor. Paldean Tauros-W's high physical bulk combined with Intimidate and Bulk Up lets it easily come in on Basculegion-M's Water-type STAB moves, but it must exercise caution against sets with Psychic Fangs.

Grass-types: Bulky Grass-types like Amoonguss and Tsareena are able to handle Basculegion-M's Water-type moves outside of rain quite effectively and can overwhelm it with their STAB moves. Amoonguss in particular can also take advantage of Basculegion-M's presence for longevity with Giga Drain and Toxic. However, both of these Pokemon must be wary of Choice Band Ice Fang, as they are vulnerable to being 2HKOed by it. Amoonguss also must look out for Psychic Fangs.

Faster Pokemon: Basculegion-M's bulk, while decent, leaves it vulnerable to various faster Pokemon with super effective coverage. Dark-types and Pokemon with Dark-type coverage such as Infernape, Cinccino, and Inteleon can all OHKO Basculegion-M with their respective Dark-type attacks after some minor chip damage. Other faster offensive Pokemon such as Tsareena, Kilowattrel, and Rotom-C can overwhelm Basculegion-M with super effective moves. However, all of these Pokemon have to be wary of Basculegion-M under rain, and non-Choice Scarf variants have to fear a possible Choice Scarf on Basculegion-M, as the majority of them are susceptible to being OHKOed by Basculegion-M's Wave Crash.

movesets.name: Substitute
movesets.description:
Set Details

Basculegion-M can opt for either a physical or special set, and they both come with their benefits and drawbacks. A physical set is more easily walled, but its Liquidation gets to come off its higher Attack. Additionally, Phantom Force being a two-turn attack means it may not always hit Basculegion-M's desired target, though it always gets a free turn of healing from Leftovers. On the other hand, a specially oriented Substitute Basculegion-M has access to reliable moves for both of its STAB types, isn't as held back by four-moveslot syndrome as physical sets are, and can surprise physical walls. However, this comes at a price of its noticeably lower Special Attack. Aqua Jet lets Basculegion-M safely pick off foes like Cinccino, Munkidori, and Infernape at low health, ensuring neither it nor its Substitute takes damage. Endeavor capitalizes on Substitute lowering Basculegion-M's HP, letting it cut down the HP of walls that it can struggle with like Vaporeon, Avalugg, and Amoonguss. On the other hand, Pain Split lets Basculegion-M simply recover some HP while simultaneously dealing damage. Leftovers is preferred, since it provides passive healing, mitigating Substitute's impact on Basculegion-M's HP. However, Metronome can capitalize on Substitute giving Basculegion-M free turns, letting it continually attack and more easily beat Vaporeon and Gastrodon, and Heavy-Duty Boots means Basculegion-M doesn't need to worry about constant chip damage from entry hazards, though this forces Basculegion-M to run Pain Split if it wishes to have any form of recovery. Jolly and Timid natures can also be used so that Basculegion-M outspeeds Tsareena, Breloom, and Toxicroak, but the wallbreaking power of Adamant and Modest is typically better. Tera Water increases the power of both Liquidation and Surf, letting Basculegion-M break through walls more easily, while Tera Dark allows it to take Ghost-type attacks from Chandelure and opposing Basculegion-M as well as Dark-type moves like Incineroar's Knock Off if necessary.

Gastrodon and Roar Vaporeon are the main roadblocks for Basculegion-M, so partners that can help pressure them like Breloom, Toxicroak, and Freeze-Dry Alolan Ninetales make for good pairings. In return, Basculegion-M can whittle down Amoonguss for Breloom as well as take care of Galarian Slowbro and Bronzong for Toxicroak and Alolan Ninetales. Pivots like Munkidori, Flygon, and Whimsicott that draw in Pokemon that Basculegion-M can set Substitute on and take advantage of, like Bronzong, Vaporeon, and Toxicroak, are greatly appreciated, though Basculegion-M must be cautious of Toxicroak's Knock Off sets. Substitute Basculegion-M sets excel at weakening defensive Water-resistant Pokemon like Amoonguss, Milotic, and Tentacruel, meaning it can pave the way for partners like Flygon, Incineroar, and Paldean Tauros-F. Avalugg is often a hard check to get past for Basculegion-M, but specially oriented sets are good at luring it in and dealing great damage. This can be capitalized on by physical attackers like Overqwil, Scyther, and Flygon. Faster Ghost-types such as Hisuian Typhlosion, Chandelure, and Brambleghast can be problematic for Basculegion-M, causing Ghost-resistant and -immune teammates like Incineroar, Scrafty, Porygon2, and Dudunsparce to be necessary. Powerful Grass-, Electric-, and Dark-type Pokemon like Breloom, Kilowattrel, and Incineroar can stop Basculegion-M from keeping up its Substitute, so checks to these Pokemon such as Amoonguss, Bellibolt, and Diancie make for good partners.

movesets.name: Rain Sweeper
movesets.description:
Set Details

Liquidation acts as a recoil-free alternative to Wave Crash at the cost of lower power. This is especially useful late-game, where Basculegion-M can wreck through weakened foes while still maintaining some health as to not be too vulnerable to revenge killers. Alternatively, Aqua Jet has more use outside of rain, being a useful priority tool to revenge kill faster Pokemon like Infernape, Munkidori, and Cinccino. For Basculegion-M's last move, it tends to opt for Tera Blast alongside Tera Ghost, as it gifts Basculegion-M a powerful and reliable physical Ghost-type STAB move to hit Water-resistant and -immune Pokemon like Vaporeon, Toxicroak, Milotic, and Tsareena. However, it forces Basculegion-M to Terastallize, so it can be off-putting at times as an option. Because of this, Psychic Fangs can be used as alternative to hit Vaporeon neutrally while also hitting checks like Toxicroak and Amoonguss super effectively. Ice Fang is another option that hits Dragon- and Grass-types like Dragalge, Tsareena, and Amoonguss attempting to switch into Basculegion-M's Water-type attacks. If not running Tera Blast, Tera Water can further boost Basculegion-M's already monstrous offensive profile, letting it 2HKO bulky Water-resistant Pokemon such as Dragalge, Amoonguss, and Tsareena with Wave Crash.

Choice Band Basculegion-M is a premier threat on rain teams thanks to its immense power and Swift Swim boosting its Speed. As a result, rain setters such as Klefki and Tornadus are necessary picks. In addition to setting rain, the former has access to a vast array of utility moves such as Thunder Wave, which cripples Choice Scarf users like Infernape and Inteleon, and Spikes, while the latter can use rain itself to break through Grass-types like Amoonguss, Wo-Chien, and Tsareena. Other Swift Swim Pokemon such as Kingdra, Overqwil, and Ludicolo have solid synergy with Basculegion-M. Kingdra can overwhelm Vaporeon, Toxicroak, and Dragalge, making it less needed for Basculegion-M to Terastallize to hit these Pokemon. Overqwil can function as a late-game cleaner that appreciates Basculegion-M's insane wallbreaking letting it finish off games more easily, as it's able to finish off weakened foes. Ludicolo's Grass-type STAB moves and Ice-type coverage can be monumental in turning the tides against bulky Water-, Grass-, and Dragon- types like Gastrodon, Vaporeon, Amoonguss, and Dragalge. Other entry hazard setters such as Gligar, Flygon, and Swampert make for good teammates, further bolstering Basculegion-M's wallbreaking capabilities.

movesets.name: All-out Attacker
movesets.description:
Set Details

Aqua Jet gives Mystic Water sets a way to pick off faster Pokemon like Chandelure, Cinccino, and Munkidori, while Liquidation helps out Choice Scarf sets by providing a less risky version of Wave Crash with more PP and no recoil. Aqua Jet can even find use on Choice Scarf variants as a means to combat faster Choice Scarf users like Munkidori. Psychic Fangs provides solid coverage, hitting Poison-types that can take Water-type moves like Dragalge, Toxicroak, and Amoonguss. Ice Fang instead targets Grass- and Dragon-types like Tsareena, Amoonguss, Flygon, and Dragalge, albeit being weaker into the aforementioned Poison-type Pokemon. Mystic Water in tandem with Adaptability makes Basculegion-M's Water-type STAB moves extremely menacing while allowing it to switch its moves. This is further boosted by Tera Water, which makes Basculegion-M's Water-type attacks monstrously strong, doing immense damage to even the bulkiest of physically defensive Pokemon like Avalugg. Alternatively, Choice Scarf patches up Basculegion-M's otherwise average Speed and makes it a formidable revenge killer in its own right. Despite this, Basculegion-M's average Speed stat prevents it from being consistent as a revenge killer, as other Choice Scarf users such as Flygon, Infernape, Munkidori, and Porygon-Z can effectively outspeed and threaten it.

All-out attacker Basculegion-M benefits many balance, bulky offense, and offense teams thanks to its ability to easily wallbreak and, if carrying Choice Scarf, its surprise factor as well. Entry hazard setters like Flygon, Swampert, and Diancie can set up Stealth Rock and Spikes, whittling down foes for Basculegion-M to more easily overwhelm. Hazard removal from the likes of Cinccino, Avalugg, and Tsareena is heavily appreciated, increasing Basculegion-M's longevity and making it more capable offensively late-game. Basculegion-M tends to draw in bulky Water- and Grass-types like Vaporeon, Amoonguss, Gastrodon, and Tsareena. As a result, offensive Pokemon that can capitalize on these foes, namely Toxicroak, Incineroar, Rotom-C, and Staraptor, can form potent wallbreaking cores with Basculegion-M. Additionally, the last three Pokemon can reliably bring Basculegion-M in with their pivot moves, giving Basculegion-M an easier time entering battle. Dark-types like Incineroar, Alolan Muk, Scrafty, and Bombirdier can counteract opposing Dark- and Ghost-types and use their presence as an opportunity to generate offensive momentum through pivoting, wearing down foes over time with Knock Off, and, in the case of the first two, status. Setup Pokemon that can boost Speed such as Dragon Dance Flygon and Tidy Up Cinccino, as well as those that increase their physical bulk like Iron Defense Registeel and Bulk Up Scrafty, can pose a problem to Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, as either Basculegion-M's average Speed stat or the lack of an additional power boost can let it down against these threats. Thus, Pokemon that can check these foes such as Orthworm, Chandelure, and Sylveon are appreciated, providing some solid defensive backbone for Basculegion-M to fall back upon. In return, these Pokemon heavily appreciate Basculegion-M's strong offensive presence.

strategies.comments:
Other Options

Tera Blast Ghost provides Basculegion physical Ghost-type coverage, but Shadow Ball tends to hit targets like Slowbro hard enough without making Basculegion reliant on exhausting a resource as valuable as Terastallization. A Choice Scarf can remedy Basculegion's mediocre Speed, but Basculegion-F generally outclasses Basculegion as a Choice Scarf user. Psychic Fangs is boosted by Choice Band, nails Amoonguss and Chesnaught, and 3HKOes Volcanion, but Basculegion is most effective as a wallbreaker across matchups when it's using all of its moveslots for its spammable STAB moves.

Checks and Counters

Water-immune Pokemon: Volcanion is a hard wall to Basculegion and prevents it from pivoting, and the threat of burns from Steam Eruption easily forces Basculegion out. Vaporeon and Storm Drain Gastrodon also outright wall Basculegion.

Bulky Water-resistant Pokemon: Chesnaught easily sponges Water-type attacks and absorbs Shadow Ball. Amoonguss and Wo-Chien can repeatedly tank Basculegion's powerful Wave Crash. Slowbro can use Regenerator to repeatedly pivot into Basculegion's Water-type attacks while threatening Basculegion with a Scald burn.

Burn: Scald users like Slowbro and Suicune can fish for burns against Basculegion. Talonflame is a relevant Flame Body user that might exhaust Terastallization or sacrifice itself to burn Basculegion for its teammates. A burn from Sacred Fire from Entei can also heavily reduce Basculegion's damage output, but does usually mean Entei is being KO'd in return if it does not Terastallize.

Faster Threats: Basculegion's tendency to wear itself out with Wave Crash recoil and entry hazard damage opens it up to revenge killers like Galarian Zapdos, Noivern, and Gengar. Priority users like Bisharp and Mimikyu even hit Basculegion super effectively.

movesets.name: Choice Band
movesets.description:
Set Details

Basculegion differentiates itself from Basculegion-F with its greater Attack, offering plenty of damage with its powerful STAB Wave Crash and other physical Water-type moves to overpower physical walls like Hippowdon and specially defensive Water-resistant Pokemon like Empoleon and Hisuian Goodra. Flip Turn helps Basculegion keep up momentum, especially against defensive switch-ins like Slowbro, Chesnaught, and Empoleon. Aqua Jet compensates for Basculegion's poor Speed and enables it to pick off faster foes like Galarian Zapdos, Krookodile, and Weak Armor-boosted Armarouge. Although Shadow Ball isn't boosted by Choice Band, it's still Basculegion's strongest move against Slowbro and only effective move against Volcanion. Adaptability cranks up Basculegion's power even further, enabling it to potentially 2HKO bulky Hisuian Goodra with Wave Crash and guaranteeing a 2HKO on Slowbro with Shadow Ball. Alternatively, Swift Swim nets Basculegion a spot on rain teams; the boost from Swift Swim compensates for Basculegion's middling Speed, and the rain provides a comparable boost to Adaptability for Basculegion's Water-type moves. Tera Water lets Basculegion's Wave Crash OHKO Cyclizar, while increasing the damage output of Aqua Jet and Flip Turn. Basculegion also enjoys shedding its weaknesses to Sucker Punch from Bisharp and Shadow Sneak from Mimikyu. The extra damage Tera Ghost provides Shadow Ball helps Adaptability variants of Basculegion finish off Slowbro more quickly, though the trade-off of losing the Adaptability boost for Basculegion's Water-type moves can make it less potent as a revenge killer and offensive pivot.

VoltTurn teams appreciate Basculegion as a powerful wallbreaker that functions as an offensive pivot, and it forms great pivot cores with Pokemon like Galarian Zapdos, Cyclizar, and Raikou. Knock Off users like Cyclizar, Hisuian Goodra, and Chesnaught threaten to cap Basculegion's damage output if they don't KO it directly, so Basculegion relies on Knock Off absorbers like Wo-Chien and Amoonguss. If Basculegion joins rain teams, it will be reliant on Politoed to get the rain up. Politoed and other Water-types on rain teams, such as Barraskewda and Kingdra, work with Basculegion to overload checks to Water-types like Slowbro and Suicune. On these rain teams, Kilowattrel can threaten bulky Water-types and Water-immune Pokemon, including Slowbro and Volcanion, for Basculegion. Healing Wish and Lunar Dance users like Jirachi, Gardevoir, and Cresselia give Basculegion a second chance wallbreaking or cleaning up, healing off any burns Basculegion's taken and making up for the massive amount of damage Basculegion tends to accrue from recoil and entry hazards. Basculegion itself appreciates hazards being up to wear down Wo-Chien and non-Heavy Duty Boots variants of Slowbro and Amoonguss, so Krookodile, Rhyperior, and Kleavor can support it. Spikes support from Chesnaught and Klefki goes even further than Stealth Rock for wearing down Hisuian Goodra, Empoleon, and other checks to Basculegion that forego Heavy-Duty Boots.

movesets.name: Offensive
movesets.description:
• With a good offensive typing and Adaptability pushing its already high-power STAB attacks past the heavens, Basculegion-M is a horrifyingly powerful wallbreaker that only gets stronger in the later stages of the game!

  • Last Respects: After just one teammate is KOed, Last Respects already becomes a strong STAB move. When it's the last Pokemon standing, this vengeful attack will 2HKO almost anything that doesn't resist it at minimum, with the big exceptions being defensive Dragonite if Multiscale is intact and Dondozo if not using Life Orb.

  • Endure and Custap Berry: Endure can be used to put Basculegion-M into Custap Berry's activation range against many powerful attacks, letting it fire off Last Respects on the top of its priority bracket. This can be a devastating surprise late-game, turning what could be a sure loss into new avenues to sweep!

  • Flip Turn: Adaptability turns Flip Turn into a powerful pivoting move, giving Basculegion-M more utility early-game.

Other Options

  • Psychic Fangs: While hitting Urshifu-R extra hard isn't a bad deal, the real use for Psychic Fangs is to get rid of dual screens that would otherwise stop Basculegion-M from sweeping.

  • Mold Breaker: Mold Breaker can be tempting for cleaving through Multiscale Dragonite, offensive Sturdy Archaludon, and the occasional Mimikyu with Last Respects, but Dragonite's habit of using Tera Normal and the big overall damage reduction makes it a rather niche option, especially since Mold Breaker announces its presence, removing any sort of surprise value.

Items

  • Life Orb: Life Orb may compromise Basculegion-M's decent bulk, but it turns the fish into an absolute scourge against bulky Pokemon, with Last Respects now 2HKOing Dondozo at its maximum power and Tera Ghost even potentially 2HKOing defensive Dragonite through Mulitscale if it lacks Leftovers!

  • Assault Vest: When used with specialized EV spreads, Basculegion-M can send common revenge killers like Flutter Mane and Gholdengo to an early grave.

  • Focus Sash: Even with Wave Crash's recoil, Focus Sash is good for winning unexpected matchups against threats like Chi-Yu and Chien-Pao, though note that this item benefits best from a more specialized set.

General EV Spreads

  • 28 HP / 252 Atk / 228 Def with Adamant: This physically bulky EV spread lets Basculegion-M survive Adamant Ogerpon-H's Horn Leech on all but the highest damage roll and does the same for Ursaluna-B's Blood Moon. It also always dodges a 2HKO from Adamant Choice Band Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes, usually survives +1 Jolly Dragonite's Scale Shot at five hits, and survives Jolly Chien-Pao's Sucker Punch.

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 252 Def with Adamant: This spread always lets Basculegion-M survive Adamant Ogerpon-H's Horn Leech, but it now has around a 19% chance of being OHKOed by Modest Ursaluna-B's Blood Moon.

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 252 Spe with Adamant: While maximizing Speed makes Basculegion-M notably frail, it does outspeed some otherwise troublesome foes like Modest Raging Bolt, although it needs to watch out for Thunderclap and the rare but deadly Adamant Breloom.

  • Brave Nature Reducing Basculegion-M's Speed can give it an edge in mirror matches when used on Trick Room teams with setters like Porygon2 and Mimikyu, but note that going as far as using a Speed IV of 0 can harm Basculegion-M's matchups against normally slower foes like Scizor, Primarina, and Corviknight, so using a Speed IV of 31 is the most flexible option.

Assault Vest EV Spreads

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 172 Def / 68 SpD / 12 Spe: This bulky spread allows Basculegion-M to avoid an OHKO from Jolly Ogerpon-H's Horn Leech, survive Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball, and outspeed paralyzed Adamant Dragonite even after one Dragon Dance.

  • 212 Atk / 244 Def / 52 SpD: This spread lets Basculegion-M survive all but the highest damage from Adamant Ogerpon-H's Horn Leech and Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball at the cost of some Attack.

  • 244 Atk / 68 SpD / 196 Spe: This enables Basculegion-M to avoid an OHKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball while still outspeeding Adamant Breloom.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Terastallization is a more of a double-edged sword than usual due to Adaptability, which only gives its damage bonus if Basculegion-M's current typing matches the attack. Because of this, while Terastallizing makes sense for Basculegion-M, it will lower the power of at least some of its attacks!

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy trades Basculegion-M's wallbreaking power for a defense against Dark-types. With Tera Blast, this can even stop Urshifu-S!

  • Water: Tera Water makes Aqua Jet a potent late-game cleaning tool and lets Basculegion-M survive most Choice Specs Flutter Mane's attacks as a bonus, with the exception of rare variants with Thunderbolt or Tera Blast Stellar.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost transforms Last Respects into a truly outrageous wallbreaking attack when Basculegion-M is the last fish swimming, with even Dondozo taking over 50% from it!

  • Fighting: Tera Fighting is a more niche option against Dark-types, leaving Basculegion-M vulnerable to Fairy-type attacks in exchange for a stronger matchup against Archaludon and Urshifu-S via Tera Blast.

  • Don't Use Tera Stellar!: Basculegion-M may seem like a perfect candidate for Tera Stellar, but don't be fooled: Adaptability has no interactions with the Stellar type, making it completely useless unless Basculegion-M is using the niche Mold Breaker!

movesets.name: Swift Swim Sweeper
movesets.description:
• With such powerful attacks and the game-ending Last Respects, Swift Swim Basculegion is the king of rain teams!

  • Last Respects: Last Respects is the key to sweeping late-game if common Water-resistant foes such as Urshifu-R are still around, but even after one teammate is KOed, it's a good coverage attack.

  • Setting Up Rain: Pelipper is almost required support for this Basculegion, not only providing the needed rain to gobble teams up but even providing Tailwind so Basculegion can outspeed extremely speedy foes like Booster Energy Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle.

  • Substitute: Substitute ruins Pokemon like Chien-Pao and Urshifu-S for daring to use Sucker Punch and helps against Raging Bolt's Thunderclap as well.

  • Head Smash: While not very reliable, this is Basculegion's most powerful attack against Dragonite and Roaring Moon and rips Iron Bundle to shreds too.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Adamant is the most reliable nature for sweeping, but Jolly does outspeed +1 Jolly Roaring Moon and Choice Scarf Latios.

  • Life Orb versus Focus Sash: Life Orb is preferred for maximizing Basculegion's late-game sweeping potential. If Life Orb is needed elsewhere, Focus Sash can be a reasonable shift in focus, making Basculegion easier to use outside of rain, which makes benching Pelipper for some matchups easier to justify.

Other Options

  • Liquidation or Waterfall: Wave Crash's constant recoil wears Basculegion down quickly, so Liquidation saves Bascluegion's scales if a foe is already in its KO range. Waterfall is a tad weaker, but the 20% chance to flinch can lead to huge upsets in a battle!

  • Rain Dance: Setting up Rain Dance usually shouldn't be a job for Basculegion, but it does severely punish Torkoal's attempt to change weather.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: While Basculegion can function without Terastalliztion, its often the star sweeper of rain teams, making it a likely choice to Terastallize.

  • Water: Tera Water boosts Wave Crash to truly obscene power, with offensive Roaring Moon in particular being OHKOed 75% of the time by Adamant Wave Crash!

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy not only saves Basculegion from Sucker Punch foes like Chien-Pao and Urshifu-S, but it also shreds Roaring Moon if it doesn't Terastallize with Tera Blast Fairy.

  • Stellar: Tera Stellar is a flexible method for sweeping, with the one-time boost to Last Respects reaping Urshifu-R's soul when Basculegion is the lone teammate alive!

  • Ghost: While it doesn't have amazing synergy with rain, Tera Ghost still boosts Last Respects into a ghoulish wallbreaking tool regardless of the weather, being particularly useful against Urshifu-R, defensive Primarina, and Dondozo

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description:
• With Choice Scarf and the powerful Adaptability-boosted Flip Turn under its fins, Basculegion is an effective revenge killer and offensive pivot with an important immunity to Extreme Speed.

  • Jolly Nature: While Adamant's power may be tempting, Jolly is needed for outspeeding Iron Bundle, Adamant Dragonite after Dragon Dance, and the rare Dragapult.

  • Last Respects: Last Respects transforms Basculegion into a vindictive sweeper once its allies have passed on to the afterlife!

  • Head Smash: While the accuracy can be worrisome, this is Basculegion's most powerful attack against Dragonite and Roaring Moon and does a reasonable job of revenge killing Choice Specs Iron Bundle when Last Respects is still weak.

  • Aqua Jet: Aqua Jet may seem ridiculous with a Choice Scarf, but it can pick off weakened priority users like Urshifu-S and Chien-Pao.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Terastallization is nice when a game-ending sweep is in sight, but reducing the power of at least one of Basculegion's STAB attacks can make it a bit situational.

  • Water: Wave Crash is the least risky move to lock Basculegion into, so Tera Water is a reasonable cleaning option.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost Last Respects is an excellent cleaning tool when Basculegion is the final soul remaining, but watch out for Ursaluna-B, Porygon2, and Tera Normal Dragonite.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy reducing the power of both STAB attacks is a big issue, but it saves Basculegion against Chien-Pao and Urshifu-S's Sucker Punch, and Tera Blast Fairy still deals good damage.

  • Don't Use Tera Stellar!: Because Adaptability does not take Tera Stellar into account, this Tera Type is fool's gold and should be ignored.

movesets.name: Agility
movesets.description:
• Agility and the terrifying Last Respects transform Basculegion into a ferocious late-game sweeper once its friends are sleeping with the fishes!

  • Last Respects and Late-game: This set is extremely focused on sweeping late-game with Agility, so while Basculegion's Water-type attacks don't make it useless earlier in the game, its best to save it as your last Pokemon to transform Last Respects into a slaughterous showstopper!

  • Wave Crash: Even if using Focus Sash, Wave Crash's power is far too good to pass up, since Basculegion isn't guaranteed to be sweeping every game.

  • Aqua Jet: A priority attack may seem pointless on a Speed boosting set, but beyond letting Basculegion revenge kill weakened Pokemon, it also ruins Sucker Punch attempts from Chien-Pao and Urshifu-S.

  • Liquidation: If using Focus Sash, Liquidation is a reasonable alternative STAB attack to let Basculegion live another day.

  • Substitute: While risky and not a great fit with Focus Sash, Substitute punishes Sucker Punch attempts from Urshifu-S and Chien-Pao and could even turn the tables on Raging Bolt's Thunderclap.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Adamant is the easiest nature to score sweeps with, but Jolly can be worth it if outspeeding Jolly +1 Roaring Moon and Choice Scarf Latios is important.

  • Focus Sash versus Life Orb: Focus Sash is the most reliable way to set up Agility, making it the best option. Life Orb can pull off sweeps with less damage though and is a reasonable alternative if another teammate already has Focus Sash.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: Terastallization guaranteeing that at least one of Basculegion's STAB attacks gets a downgrade is a bummer, but this set focuses so heavily on late-game sweeping that it's likely to go that route regardless.

  • Ghost: Even though Tera Ghost doesn't offer much defensive benefit, boosting Last Respects is often a key ingredient for sweeping.

  • Water: Tera Water gives Basculegion more flexibility in sweeping without the lives of its teammates being over, though Last Respects can become a disappointing cleaning tool later in the match.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy provides insurance against Sucker Punch throwers like Urshifu-S and Chien-Pao, but both STAB attacks receiving a power downgrade is a big problem. If doing this, seriously consider Tera Blast to rip Dark-types to shreds.

  • Don't Use Tera Stellar!: Tera Stellar is a siren song, having no impact on Basculegion's power at all due to Adaptability's mechanics.

movesets.name: Rain Sweeper
movesets.description:
========

  • Basculegion-M functions as a powerful sweeper under rain, using Swift Swim in tandem with its powerful STAB moves to outspeed and threaten many common metagame threats, including Calyrex-S, Calyrex-I, Chi-Yu, and Incineroar, among others.
  • Last Respects becomes incredibly powerful after one or two teammates have fainted, most notably being able to OHKO Whimsicott after two partners have fainted, making it a very high value move for Basculegion-M. Aqua Jet provides priority for Basculegion-M, dealing sizeable damage with both rain and Life Orb while being able to KO low health foes.
  • Life Orb allows Basculegion-M to OHKO Calyrex-I with 150-Base Power Last Respects and Incineroar under rain with Wave Crash after Intimidate.
  • The Speed investment allows Basculegion-M to outspeed Calyrex-S and Choice Scarf Chi-Yu when in the rain, while the Defense investment lets it survive Incineroar's Knock Off and Rillaboom's Grassy Glide. The Attack investment allows Basculegion-M to OHKO offensive Lunala with 100-Base Power Last Respects and bulky Miraidon with 150-Base Power Last Respects.
  • Tera Ghost boosts the output of Last Respects significantly, notably allowing Basculegion-M to OHKO Calyrex-I with 100-Base Power Last Respect swhile also removing its weakness to Grass- and Electric-type moves, notably Grassy Glide, Thunderclap, and Miraidon's Volt Switch.

Teambuilding

  • Amoonguss and Ogerpon-C are both very problematic for Basculegion-M, as they can safely redirect its attacks, allowing for a partner to hit it freely, while Ogerpon-C can easily threaten it with Power Whip.
  • Raging Bolt, Chien-Pao, and Rillaboom can all threaten Basculegion-M with super effective priority moves in Thunderclap, Sucker Punch, and Grassy Glide while being able to take its attacks in return.
  • Miraidon can comfortably take Basculegion-M's attacks while threatening it back with an OHKO with Electro Drift, whereas Koraidon can replace the rain with sun, hindering it. Focus Sash Calyrex-S can take a hit from Basculegion-M and easily KO it back with Astral Barrage.
  • Kyogre pairs amazingly with Basculegion-M, as it can set rain to activate Swift Swim while having very powerful spread damage in Water Spout and Origin Pulse that can help against the redirection users that are problematic for Basculegion-M. In return, Basculegion-M can threaten faster Pokemon like Ogerpon-H, Urshifu-R, and Calyrex-S that can threaten Kyogre.
  • Calyrex-I also pairs very well with Basculegion-M, as it can hit the Grass- and Dragon-types that can take Basculegion-M’s hits like Rillaboom, Miraidon, and Raging Bolt with Glacial Lance. In return, Basculegion-M can hit the Fire- and Ghost-types that threaten Calyrex-I, like Incineroar and Calyrex-S.
  • Amoonguss supports Basculegion-M very well, with redirection from Rage Powder protecting Basculegion-M from powerful attacks, notably priority such as Sucker Punch; it is also able to put foes to sleep with Spore, allowing Basculegion-M to attack safely. Basculegion-M, in return, hits the Fire- and Psychic-types that threaten Amoonguss such as Chi-Yu and Calyrex-S.
  • Basculegion-M appreciates damage reduction, notably from Grimmsnarl in the form of dual screens and from Incineroar in the form of Intimidate, which allows it to more safely output damage. In return, Basculegion-M matches up very well against Urshifu-R, which can bypass both’s damage reduction.

strategies.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Swift Swim sets only appear on rain teams, as otherwise Basculegion-M would be playing without an ability. The Choice Scarf Adaptability set typically appears on balance teams that benefit heavily from getting a quick OHKO against foes like Incineroar. The Focus Sash set can fit on either balance teams or on rain teams with speed control options, as it appreciates rain boosting the weaker Liquidation. Both the Choice Scarf and Focus Sash Adaptability sets can still benefit heavily from being on a rain team thanks to the Water-type damage amplification, despite not having Swift Swim.
  • Pelipper’s Drizzle ability allows Swift Swim Basculegion-M to outspeed nearly the entire metagame, as well as boosting the damage of its Water-type attacks, while Pelipper itself can pressure opposing Grass-types with Hurricane. Archaludon can cover Basculegion-M’s weakness to Dark-type Pokemon such as Kingambit using Body Press, round out the offensive core of a rain team, and serve as a bulky pivot to be sent out after using Flip Turn, resisting attacks from Rillaboom and Kilowattrel.
  • Incineroar can be used to ensure Rillaboom’s Grassy Glide will never OHKO even if Rillaboom has Miracle Seed and stop opposing Basculegion-M from getting an OHKO with unboosted Last Respects.
  • Amoonguss and Sinistcha can use Rage Powder to redirect attacks that threaten to OHKO Basculegion-M, such as Kingambit’s Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave, while improving the team’s matchup against Trick Room. Additionally, Sinistcha's Hospitality and Life Dew can be used to bring Basculegion-M back to full health to make use of Focus Sash, stay out of range of attacks like Grassy Glide from Rillaboom, and heal recoil damage from Wave Crash.
  • Grass-type Pokemon like Amoonguss and Rillaboom stop Basculegion-M from sweeping through teams with Wave Crash, as Amoonguss can redirect and resist the attack, while Rillaboom is always threatening an OHKO with Wood Hammer. Pelipper can use Hurricane to hit these Pokemon for massive damage, or Basculegion-M outside of rain teams can be paired with Fire-types like Volcarona and Talonflame. Dark-type Pokemon like Incineroar and Kingambit threaten an OHKO against Basculegion-M and prevent it from sweeping with Last Respects, making Close Combat Sneasler a worthwhile partner. A Commander-boosted Dondozo can survive multiple Last Respects and resist any Water-type attacks. Archaludon can threaten Dondozo with Electro Shot, and Pelipper can punish Tera Grass Dondozo with Hurricane. Alternatively, teams can use Incineroar and Rillaboom along with Basculegion-M's Flip Turn to cycle Intimidate and Fake Out, or Multiscale Dragonite to safely remove Dondozo's stat boosts with Haze. Alolan Ninetales pairs well with the Choice Scarf set because it can hit Grass-types with Blizzard and Water-types like Dondozo with Freeze-Dry, while Basculegion-M covers for Alolan Ninetales's weakness to Fire-type Pokemon such as Incineroar. Opposing Archaludon are unlikely to be knocked out even by a maximum power Last Resepcts, so Fighting-type coverage from Annihilape and Sneasler and Ground-type coverage from Ursaluna-B is appreciated.

Strategy Comments

  • Basculegion-M functions as a late-game cleaner or early-game wallbreaker with high Speed and damage. The Swift Swim sets need its team to set up rain to activate Swift Swim, or else it can be taken out by a quicker foe. It can secure endgames with high-Base Power Last Respects if its teammates have done enough damage to the opposing team. It can bail out of positions with Flip Turn while its teammates take out the foes that are preventing it from sweeping. In the early-game, it can remove the Ursaluna formes, which can allow a teammate like Archaludon to sweep.
  • Basculegion-M can be used early or late in a battle, but it must be saved for the late-game if maximizing the damage of Last Respects is necessary. It can be used effectively in the early-game by knocking out a Pokemon such as Incineroar, which can allow a teammate like Gholdengo to sweep the opposing team. The Focus Sash set can clinch an endgame using combinations of Liquidation and Last Respects, but the Choice item sets must be more careful to leave foes that can be swept by one move for last.
  • Sun teams can mitigate Basculegion-M’s Speed and offense, particularly for the Swift Swim set. Pokemon that set up sun upon switching in like Torkoal can be countered by keeping Pelipper in the back and switching it in when sun is up to overwrite it. Manual sun setters like Whimsicott must be taken out by a teammate like Incineroar with Flare Blitz or Archaludon with Flash Cannon, as switching in Pelipper will set up rain first, which will be canceled by Whimsicott’s Sunny Day. Alolan Ninetales can change rain to snow, take a hit from Basculegion-M and return damage with Freeze-Dry, and use Disable to nullify a Choice item set or Aurora Veil to mitigate its damage output. Basculegion-M can use Flip Turn to reposition until rain is set, and Pelipper can be lead into Alolan Ninetales because it is slower and so will activate Drizzle after Snow Warning, though an Alolan Ninetales in the back can still switch in to cancel rain. Tyranitar can overwrite rain with Sand Stream and can switch into Last Respects while breaking Focus Sash. Pelipper should expect to be faster than Tyranitar, so sand will be set up after rain. Thus, Pelipper is more likely to successfully set rain if it is reserved in the back or if Tyranitar is knocked out by Basculegion-M's teammates.

movesets.name: Rain Sweeper
movesets.description:
• Basculegion-M uses its high-Base Power STAB attacks like Wave Crash and Last Respects to claim knockouts in the early-game and secure wins in the late-game, respectively, as well as its Swift Swim ability to outspeed nearly the whole unboosted metagame under rain, giving it positive matchups against metagame staples such as Incineroar, Gholdengo, and Volcarona.
  • Last Respects can reach an incredible Base Power of 200, threatening nearly every Pokemon that does not resist Ghost-type attacks with an OHKO. Aqua Jet allows Basculegion-M to pick off a foe at low health while avoiding Sucker Punch from Kingambit. Flip Turn allows it to deal damage and retreat to safety before being attacked.
  • Choice Band maximizes Basculegion-M’s damage, notably improving the chance for Last Respects with two fainted teammates to OHKO Rillaboom.
  • Tera Water maximizes the damage output of Basculegion-M's Water-type attacks, guaranteeing an OHKO against almost any Gholdengo set, and removes its weakness to Dark-type attacks such as Kingambit’s Sucker Punch. Tera Grass allows Basculegion-M to survive any attack from Rillaboom, resist Electro Shot from Archaludon, and ignore Spore and Rage Powder from Amoonguss.
  • The defensive investment allows Basculegion-M to survive a Grassy Glide from Rillaboom. With the Attack investment, Basculegion-M will always OHKO Incineroar in the rain with Wave Crash even after Intimidate. The Speed investment allows it to always outspeed Primarina.
  • Choice-locked sets are inherently more risky to use, as being locked into the wrong move can lose an endgame. The Swift Swim set is riskier in terms of speed control, as it relies on its team to set up rain. This set has the potential to be faster than the Choice Scarf set, but without rain, its Speed and damage output can be underwhelming. It has the advantage of Choice Band providing a higher damage boost than Adaptability. This set, as well as the Choice Scarf set, are risky to use over the Focus Sash set as they can be knocked out with one hit.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf Sweeper
movesets.description:
• Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can be used on a team that does not have a way to set up rain to outspeed foes in any situation. Adaptability can make up for the decreased damage output. This set can finish off damaged teams with Last Respects without needing a Speed boost from rain.
  • Because of Choice Scarf, Basculegion-M is likely to outspeed its foes, so it can use Flip Turn to switch into a bulkier ally when threatened. Tera Blast is only intended for the Tera Fighting set, in order to hit Kingambit and Archaludon.
  • Tera Water can be used to amplify Basculegion-M's damage. Tera Fighting is used with Tera Blast to pressure Kingambit with an OHKO while resisting its Sucker Punch, and it also lets Basculegion-M resist Knock Off from Incineroar and Tyranitar.
  • A Jolly nature with maximum Speed is necessary for the Choice Scarf set to outspeed Dragapult.
  • Adaptability is always useful due to always providing a boost in some way, whereas Swift Swim is contingent on rain being active for Basculegion-M to benefit. However, this set will not do as much damage as the Choice Band set. The Choice Scarf set may not perform well against opposing speed control such as Trick Room, as it cannot use Protect to stall out turns of Trick Room.

movesets.name: Focus Sash Sweeper
movesets.description:
• The Focus Sash set allows Basculegion-M to take a hit and return with strong attacks such as Liquidation and Last Respects.
  • Liquidation is used over Wave Crash in order to avoid taking recoil damage and breaking Focus Sash.
  • Tera Ghost is used with this set, as Last Respects is likely to become stronger than its weaker Water-type attacks.
  • This set can survive a fast attack under Tailwind or Trick Room and use Protect to stall them out, making it generally better against opposing speed control compared to the other sets. However, it will not do as much damage as the Choice Band set and is unlikely to be able to threaten an early-game OHKO because it lacks Wave Crash. It can fit on a variety of teams due to it being self-sufficient in terms of damage output and not necessarily needing speed control.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 5 onwards

Price Range: 8-9 points

Overview: Both Basculegion formes are strong wallbreakers and solid late-game sweepers, most commonly used when supported by rain thanks to solid STAB attacks like Hydro Pump and Wave Crash. However, Adaptability allows them to become threatening attackers even without rain support. Picking Basculegion formes provides the drafter flexibility; Basculegion-F excels in matchups where Special Attack is preferred and against Ghost-weak teams, while Basculegion-M excels in matchups where Wave Crash is very spammable. Both formes' middling Speed outside of rain does mean they require specific support from their teammates to truly excel. Furthermore, they find themselves competing with other, faster rain sweepers and wallbreakers, which means that they're rarely your first choice for either of their roles.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Swift Swim Sweeper: Both Basculegion formes become extremely hard-hitting threats under rain, outspeeding the entire unboosted metagame and a good portion of the boosted metagame as well. With their high-powered Water-type STAB moves further boosted by the rain, they can threaten OHKOs or punch holes for their teammates.

Wallbreaker: Both Basculegion formes' access to Adaptability, combined with their high-Base Power STAB moves, can make for a potent wallbreaker. Using a Choice or damage-boosting item enhances their wallbreaking potential further. They also have access to Flip Turn, allowing them to retain momentum for their teammates and dent physical walls switching in.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Wave Crash, Hydro Pump, Liquidation, Shadow Ball, Phantom Force, Aqua Jet, Surf

Setup Moves: Agility

Utility Moves: Flip Turn, Substitute, Pain Split

Coverage: Crunch, Head Smash, Ice Beam, Ice Fang, Psychic Fangs, Tera Blast

Niche Moves

Rain Dance: Rain Dance allows both Basculegion formes to set up rain in a pinch, enabling it them to outspeed the entire unboosted metagame and punch holes for their teammates.

Common Items

Choice Band / Choice Specs: Both Choice Band and Choice Specs are commonly used to amplify both Basculegion formes' wallbreaking potential to even further heights.

Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf is more commonly used when both Basculegion formes are not paired with weather to shore up their middling Speed. This allows them to act as revenge killers or late-game sweepers without needing a turn to set up.

Damage-boosting Items: Damage-boosting items are more commonly run when Basculegion's formes want to switch their moves but still retain the power to punch holes or sweep through an opposing team.

Niche Items

Resistance Berries: One-time resistance Berries can be used to take a super effective attack and, in return, set up or take out the foe.

Heavy-Duty Boots: Heavy-Duty Boots can be run in matchups where Basculegion's formes are expected to come in frequently and do not benefit from a damage boost.

Tera

Both Basculegion formes are solid Tera users. Offensive Tera types such as Tera Water and Ghost boost their STAB moves to even more frightening amounts of damage, and Tera Ghost also gives Basculegion-M access to a physical Ghost-type STAB move in Tera Blast. On the other hand, Tera Electric and Fighting allow both Basculegion formes to muscle past natural defensive answers, such as bulky Water- and Dark-types, respectively. Adaptability also works well with Tera, giving Basculegion's formes an extra punch on their new type. However, this does mean they lose the Adaptability boost on their original typings. The major drawback of using Tera with Basculegion's formes is that it locks you out of selecting a top-tier Tera Captain, which usually benefits from Tera far more than Basculegion's formes would.

Draft Strategy

Both Basculegion formes are solid wallbreakers with options to pivot for their team. They are most commonly seen on rain teams, as that allows them to make full use of their kits. This means you should not draft them without dedicated team support, as they need it to fully function.

Rain Setters: Basculegion's formes are best utilized with teammates to set up rain for them. This allows them to be used to their full potential, as rain both shores up their middling Speed and boosts their Water-type STAB moves even further. Pelipper is the most common teammate here, as it doesn't need a turn to set rain.

Late-game Cleaners: Both Basculegion formes excel at punching holes for their teammates, so a teammate that can make solid use of this is often appreciated. Furthermore, you can reverse these roles by having this teammate punch holes for Basculegion's formes to exploit. Iron Valiant, Darkrai, and Serperior all appreciate both Basculegion formes' ability to punch holes for them.

Slow Pivots: Basculegion's formes' middling bulk means they do not like hard-switching into moves. Thus, a slow pivot that can bring it them in safely is much appreciated. Scizor, Corviknight, and Iron Hands all help Basculegion's formes in one way or another.

Entry Hazard Control: Both Basculegion formes appreciate strong entry hazard control from their teammates. Considering they tend to take some recoil damage or hits when they come in, having strong hazard control ensures a bit more longevity, allowing them to do their job without being locked into running Heavy-Duty Boots. Great Tusk, Corviknight, and Cyclizar all help out with this, with Great Tusk threatening the Dark-types that naturally beat Basculegion's formes.

Defensive Teammates: Basculegion's formes basically provide no defensive utility, barring their Ghost typing allowing them to switch into Fighting-type moves. This means that other teammates should pick up the slack. Those teammates are especially useful if they can compress the roles that both Basculegion formes need to function. Great Tusk, Corviknight, and Archuladon all are great defensive teammates that help Basculegion's formes function.

Checks and Counters

Strong Priority Users: Both Basculegion formes are vulnerable to several forms of priority, including Sucker Punch from Kingambit and Meowscarada, Grassy Glide from Rillaboom, and Thunderclap from Raging Bolt.

Faster Pokemon: Neither Basculegion forme is exactly the bulkiest of Pokemon. This means that they are vulnerable to getting OHKOed by foes that are faster than them, be it Choice Scarf users when they are in rain or threatening wallbreakers out of rain. Choice Scarf Darkrai and Choice Scarf Weavile both outspeed Basculegion's formes in rain, and Urshifu-S and Kyurem both outspeed them out of rain.

Water-resistant Pokemon: Basculegion-M struggles to hit Water-resistant foes due to its lack of secondary STAB moves and solid coverage. This means that bulky Water-types can attempt to halt it in its tracks. Empoleon, Rotom-W, and Ogerpon-W all can act as solid defensive options.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf Sweeper
movesets.description:
• Basculegion-M is a niche sweeper on hyper offense teams, primarily those utilizing Psychic Terrain and Sticky Web, due to its mediocre Speed tier and susceptibility to priority moves. Basculegion-M’s viability is tied to it being the strongest user of Last Respects, letting it OHKO or 2HKO almost the entire tier when it's the last Pokemon. Bulky Ghost-resistant Pokemon such as Yveltal and Arceus-Dark can also be 2HKOed by 300-Base Power Last Respects, leaving only Arceus as a safe switch-in. While fast, Basculegion-M is still outsped by Zacian-C and Deoxys-S, so it can only sweep once both of those Pokemon have fainted.
  • Wave Crash lets Basculegion-M wear down Arceus, 2HKOing it after Stealth Rock damage. Tera Blast Fighting puts even more pressure on Arceus, being able to OHKO it after some chip damage while also 2HKOing bulkier variants of Arceus-Dark, which is important because both otherwise prevent Last Respects from being a roll.
  • Flip Turn can be used to generate momentum if Arceus switches in or if Arceus-Dark or Yveltal switch in if Last Respects is not at full power. Aqua Jet lets Basculegion-M pick off threats like a weakened Arceus-Ground that outspeeds it after a Dragon Dance.
  • Tera Fighting makes Basculegion-M resistant to Yveltal’s Sucker Punch and neutral to Marshadow's Shadow Sneak, preventing it from being revenge killed by them; it also synergizes best with Tera Blast to hit Arceus harder than Wave Crash.
  • Basculegion-M should almost always be sent out once most, if not all, of its teammates have fainted, maximizing Last Respect’s power. Generally, using Basculegion-M is fairly straightforward, as 300-Base Power Last Respects should OHKO everything left, but it has to Terastallize in order to beat a healthy defensive Yveltal or Arceus-Dark. If Arceus is on the opposing team, the main priority would be to either KO it with a partner like Arceus-Ground or Deoxys-A or poison it such as with Glimmora's Toxic Spikes, limiting its longevity.
  • Due to Basculegion-M’s susceptibility to priority, it functions best on Psychic Spam teams utilizing Tapu Lele and Deoxys-A to punch holes early on. Glimmora is a solid partner, as it can set Toxic Spikes and Spikes to wear down Arceus and Arceus-Dark, enabling Basculegion to sweep in the late game.
  • Sticky Web teams with Shuckle or Smeargle can also utilize Basculegion, as the Sticky Webs let Basculegion outspeed Deoxys-A and Zacian-C, as well as other boosted Pokemon. Wallbreakers such as Swords Dance Necrozma-DM and Ultra Necrozma are great partners, as they lure and remove both Yveltal and Arceus-Dark easily.
  • While Basculegion-M is strong, it is still unable to OHKO extremely physically bulky Pokemon such as Zygarde-C and defensive Primal Groudon, so the aforementioned entry hazards help wear them down, alongside teammates that put pressure on them like Taunt Arceus-Ground and Zacian-C.

movesets.name: Swift Swim
movesets.description:
• The given EV spread allows Basculegion to survive Grassy Slide from Rillaboom and outspeed scarfed Chi-Yu during Rain or Tailwind.
  • Tera Grass helps Basculegion to avoid super effective damage from priority users such as Raging Bolt and Rillaboom while also preventing Amoonguss from redirecting Basculegion's attacks or putting it to sleep.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description: • Jolly nature is required to outspeed Flutter Mane.
